questions.question_text: Volatile oil from Lemon peels contains d-limonene which is
questions.explanation: d-Limonene is a well-known monocyclic terpene containing a six-membered ring with one double bond and an isopropenyl group.

questions.question_text: In case of Digitalis purpurea, the cardiac activity is maximum with
questions.explanation: Purpurea glycoside A is the primary genuine glycoside found in Digitalis purpurea containing glucose attached to digitoxin.

questions.question_text: Dragendorff's reagent does not give positive test with
questions.explanation: Caffeine is a purine alkaloid (xanthine derivative) that lacks basic properties typical of true alkaloids and typically fails to precipitate with Dragendorff's reagent.

questions.question_text: The instrument used to measure particle volume is
questions.explanation: The Coulter Counter measures the volume of particles based on the electrical resistance change as particles pass through an aperture.

questions.question_text: The purpose of seal coating in sugar coating process for tablets is

options.A: To prevent moisture penetration into the tablet core
options.B: To round the edges and build up the tablet weight
options.C: To impart the desired color to the tablet
options.D: To give lusture to the tablet

questions.explanation: Seal coating forms a water-impermeable barrier around the tablet core to protect it from moisture during subsequent aqueous coating steps.

questions.question_text: The phenomenon of increasing the solubility of weak electrolytes and non polar molecules by the addition of water miscible solvent in which the drug has good solubility is called
questions.explanation: Cosolvency refers to the addition of a water-miscible solvent in which a poorly soluble drug is more soluble, thereby enhancing its total solubility.

questions.question_text: HLB system is used to classify
questions.explanation: The Hydrophilic-Lipophilic Balance (HLB) scale is used to characterize the relative polarity of surfactants.

questions.question_text: The statement "Store in a cool place" as per IP, means

options.C: Store at any temperature between $8^{\circ}$ to $25^{\circ}$ C

questions.explanation: According to the Indian Pharmacopoeia, a cool place denotes a temperature between $8^{\circ}$ and $25^{\circ}$ C.

questions.question_text: Durability of a tablet to combined effects of shock and abrasion is evaluated by using
questions.explanation: A friabilator determines the resistance of tablets to mechanical shock and abrasion during manufacturing, packing, and shipping.

questions.question_text: Ion exchange capacity of a resin is dependent on

options.A: The total molecular weight of the resin
options.B: The total number of ion active groups
options.D: Solubility of the ion exchange resins

questions.explanation: The exchange capacity is directly proportional to the number of functional ion-active groups available per unit weight or volume.

questions.question_text: In mass spectra, the most intense peak is the
questions.explanation: The base peak corresponds to the most abundant ion formed in the mass spectrum, assigned a relative intensity of 100%.

questions.question_text: Chemical shift is expressed in one of the following units
questions.explanation: Chemical shift in NMR spectroscopy is standardly expressed in parts per million (ppm).

questions.question_text: Xenon arc lamp is the source of light in
questions.explanation: Xenon arc lamps provide high-intensity continuous radiation in the UV-visible range and are commonly used in spectrofluorimeters.

questions.question_text: Which of the following pairs has an interaction beneficial for routine clinical use
questions.explanation: Antacids like aluminum hydroxide can increase the rate of absorption of pseudoephedrine due to alkalinization of the stomach.

questions.question_text: Measurement of which of the following two of the constituents of human plasma is of great value in the differential diagnosis of rheumatoid diseases
questions.explanation: Rheumatoid factor and C-reactive protein (CRP) are classic clinical markers assessed together for the diagnosis and monitoring of rheumatoid diseases.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is valid comparison of live attenuated vaccines versus killed inactivated vaccines

options.A: Hypersensitivity reactions are uncommon among inactivated vaccines
options.B: Live attenuated vaccines are more effective in children
options.C: Live attenuated vaccines are not suitable for pediatrics use
options.D: Replication of the organisms in a live attenuated vaccine increases the stimulation of the immune system there by requiring a lower dose

questions.explanation: Live attenuated vaccines replicate in the host, providing prolonged antigenic exposure and strong immunity, typically requiring smaller doses than inactivated ones.

questions.question_text: An antineoplastic agent acting by folate antagonism and having a pteridine ring is
questions.explanation: Methotrexate is a well-known antifolate antineoplastic agent containing a pteridine ring structure.

questions.question_text: One of the following drugs has 1,4-dihydropyridine structure, tertiary amino group in the side chain and $Ca^{++}$ channel antagonist action
questions.explanation: Nicardipine is a 1,4-dihydropyridine calcium channel blocker that possesses a basic tertiary amino group in its ester side chain.

questions.question_text: IUPAC name for one of the steroidal anti-inflammatory agent is 9-$\alpha$-Fluoro-$11\beta$, $16\alpha$, $17\alpha$, 21-tetrahydroxy-1,4-Pregnadiene-3,20-dione
questions.explanation: This specific stereochemical IUPAC nomenclature corresponds to triamcinolone.

questions.question_text: CLOFAZIMINE belongs to a class of
questions.explanation: Clofazimine is an anti-leprosy drug belonging structurally to the class of riminophenazines.

questions.question_text: One of the drug is odd one in terms of its biological action
questions.explanation: Tamoxifen is an estrogen receptor antagonist (SERM), whereas diethylstilbestrol, ethynyl estradiol, and mestranol are estrogen receptor agonists.

questions.question_text: The key intermediates for the synthesis of TIMOLOL are
questions.explanation: Timolol synthesis utilizes 3,4-dichloro-1,2,5-thiadiazole reacted with morpholine derivatives.

questions.question_text: One of the following drug interrupts the synthesis of thyroid hormones bypreventing iodine incorporation into the tyrosyl residue of thyroglobulin
questions.explanation: Propylthiouracil inhibits thyroid peroxidase, preventing the iodination of tyrosyl residues on thyroglobulin.

questions.question_text: Macrolide antibiotics exert their action by
questions.explanation: Macrolides bind to the 50S ribosomal subunit, inhibiting translocation and leading to premature peptide chain dissociation/termination.

questions.question_text: One of the following is selective $\beta_2$-stimulant
questions.explanation: Salbutamol is a well-known short-acting selective $\beta_2$ adrenergic receptor agonist used as a bronchodilator.

questions.question_text: Cascaroside A is an example of
questions.explanation: Cascarosides are unique anthraquinone glycosides that contain both O-glycosidic and C-glycosidic linkages.

questions.question_text: Precursor of the biosynthesis of Tropane group of alkaloids is
questions.explanation: Tropane alkaloids are biosynthetically derived from the amino acid ornithine (via putrescine and N-methylpyrrolinium cation).

questions.question_text: The extraction of steroidal saponins on commercial scale is from
questions.explanation: Dioscorea species are the primary commercial source for diosgenin, a crucial starting material for steroidal saponins and hormones.

questions.question_text: Rauwalfia sepentina Benth., can be distinguished from other adulterants/ substitutes of Rauwolfia spp. by
questions.explanation: The characteristic presence of stone cells (sclereids) helps differentiate authentic Rauwolfia serpentina from certain adulterants.

questions.question_text: Schedule FF contains the list of the following

options.A: Drug which can be marketed under generic names only
options.D: Drug which are exempt from certain provisions applicable to manufacturing

questions.explanation: Schedule FF under the Drugs and Cosmetics Act prescribes standards for ophthalmic preparations.

questions.question_text: One of the following equations is used to predict the stability of a drug product at room temperature from experiments at accelerated temperature
questions.explanation: The Arrhenius equation describes the temperature dependence of reaction rates, allowing shelf-life prediction at room temperature from accelerated testing.

questions.question_text: One of the following apparatus is used to determine the particle size by the gravity sedimentation method
questions.explanation: The Andreasen pipette apparatus is a classic device used to measure particle size distribution via gravitational sedimentation.

questions.question_text: One of the following mills works on both the principles of attrition and impact
questions.explanation: Hammer mills operate primarily through impact, but attrition also contributes to particle size reduction as material brushes against the screen and hammers.

questions.question_text: A commonly used antioxidant for oil system is
questions.explanation: Butylated hydroxytoluene (BHT) is a lipophilic phenolic antioxidant widely used to protect oils and fats from auto-oxidation.

questions.question_text: In Digitalis glycoside $C_{17}$ position of the steroidal ring is substituted by
questions.explanation: Cardiotonic steroids (cardenolides) feature an unsaturated five-membered lactone ring (butenolide) attached at the $C_{17}$ position.

questions.question_text: Metoprolol is sometimes preferred to Propranolol because

options.A: It has both $\alpha$ and $\beta$ adrenergic blockade
options.B: It has both vasodilator properties and betaadrenergic blocker
options.C: It is a $\beta_1$ selective antagonist and it does not enter the brain

questions.explanation: Metoprolol is a cardioselective $\beta_1$ receptor blocker, making it less likely to cause bronchoconstriction compared to non-selective blockers like propranolol.

questions.question_text: The major product formed by the condensation of 2-trifluorl methyl phenothiazine with sodamide and 1-(3chlororopyl-1-4-methyl piperazine)
questions.explanation: This specific synthetic pathway yields trifluoperazine, a phenothiazine antipsychotic with a trifluoromethyl group and a methylpiperazine side chain.

questions.question_text: One of the following statements is characteristic for natural estrogens

options.A: Aromatic ring with phenolic group and an estrange nucleus
options.B: Aromatic ring with an alcoholic group and a pregnant nucleus
options.C: Reduced ring system belonging to the class estrange
options.D: Reduced ring system belonging to the class pregnane

questions.explanation: Natural estrogens possess an aromatic ring A with a phenolic hydroxyl group at C3 and belong to the estrane (18-carbon) steroid skeleton.

questions.question_text: One of the following opioid peptides is released from pro-opio melanocortin (POMC)
questions.explanation: Beta-endorphin is an endogenous opioid peptide derived from the pro-opiomelanocortin (POMC) precursor molecule in the pituitary gland.

questions.question_text: The ultra short-acting barbiturates have brief duration of action due to

options.A: High degree of binding to plasma protein
options.B: Low lipid solubility resulting in a minimal concentration in the brain
options.C: Metabolism is slow in the liver
options.D: Rapid rate of redistribution from the brain due to its high liposubility

questions.explanation: Ultra short-acting barbiturates like thiopental are highly lipophilic, causing them to rapidly cross the blood-brain barrier and subsequently redistribute quickly into muscle and fat tissues.

questions.question_text: Derivasation is done in GC

options.A: To convert a less polar compound to a more polar compound
options.C: To convert a polar compound to a more polar compound

questions.explanation: Derivatization in gas chromatography is typically performed to enhance volatility and thermal stability, though sometimes polar/functional groups are modified for better separation.

questions.question_text: Qualitative analysis by polarography is based on
questions.explanation: In polarography, the half-wave potential ($E_{1/2}$) is characteristic of a specific electroactive species, making it useful for qualitative identification.

questions.question_text: The stationary phase used in gel permeation chromatography is
questions.explanation: Styrene-divinylbenzene copolymers are commonly employed as porous gel beads for size exclusion (gel permeation) chromatography.

questions.question_text: A conductivity cell consists of
questions.explanation: A standard conductivity cell uses two platinized platinum electrodes to measure the electrical conductance of electrolyte solutions accurately.

questions.question_text: A typical example of exotoxin is
questions.explanation: Tetanospasmin is a potent neurotoxin produced by Clostridium tetani, representing a classic bacterial exotoxin.

questions.question_text: A specimen isolated form a patient suffering from septicemia was found to be a strict aerobe. Its culture vial had a characteristic grape like odour and it was susceptible to carbenicillin. Identify the organism
questions.explanation: Pseudomonas aeruginosa is characterized by a distinctive grapaelike or corn tortilla-like odor, is a strict aerobe, and is typically susceptible to antipseudomonal penicillins like carbenicillin.

questions.question_text: The pKa of lidocaine is 7.9. if the pH of the infected is 8.9, the fraction of the drug in the ionized form will be
questions.explanation: Using the Henderson-Hasselbalch equation for a weak base: $\text{pH} = \text{p}K_a + \log([\text{Unionized}]/[\text{Ionized}])$. With $\text{pH} - \text{p}K_a = 1.0$, the ratio of unprotonated to protonated is 10:1, meaning 10% is ionized.

questions.question_text: The drug regimen useful in the treatment of both intestinal and extra-intestinal symptoms of amoebiasis orally is
questions.explanation: Metronidazole treats both intestinal and extra-intestinal (hepatic) amoebiasis, while a luminal amoebicide like diloxanide furoate is given concurrently to clear luminal infection.

questions.question_text: The drug NIFEDIPINE can be synthesized from

options.A: O-nitro benzaldehyde methyl acetoacetate and ammonia
options.B: P-nitro benzaldehyde methyl acetoacetate and ammonia
options.C: O-nitro benzaldehyde ethyl acetoacetate and methylamine
options.D: P-nitro benzaldehyde methyl acetoacetate and methylamine

questions.explanation: Nifedipine is synthesized via a Hantzsch dihydropyridine condensation reaction using o-nitrobenzaldehyde, methyl acetoacetate, and ammonia.

questions.question_text: Methyl malonyl CoA mutase which catalyzes the conversion of propionyl CoA to succinyl utilizes the prosthetic group derived from
questions.explanation: Methylmalonyl-CoA mutase requires coenzyme B12, which is a derivative of cyanocobalamin (Vitamin B12).

questions.question_text: Assign the bands in the IR spectrum for appropriate groups given below: $>C=O$, Aromatic compound, $-OH$, $>C=<$, $-C 	riangledown C-$. (a) $3700-3500 \text{ cm}^{-1}$ (b) $1740-1720 \text{ cm}^{-1}$ (c) $1667-1640 \text{ cm}^{-1}$ (d) $2260-2100 \text{ cm}^{-1}$ (e) $900-675 \text{ cm}^{-1}$
questions.explanation: Stretching frequency $3700-3500 \text{ cm}^{-1}$ corresponds to the hydroxyl ($-OH$) group in IR spectroscopy.
